notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. Brooks is a first-time candidate (retired Bethlehem firefighter, union leader) with no prior public office, so there are no official-office records. The campaign site could not be reached through search results and was not opened. The only quoted material on AI-adjacent topics comes from a Townhall (conservative-leaning) article quoting his @VoteBobBrooks X posts; the page was opened, but the text was returned through a page-summarising fetch tool, so the reviewer should confirm exact wording. Other posts quoted there: 26 September 2026 'Mackenzie cashes Big Tech's checks and then votes to support more data centers in our communities' (also D). Townhall also paraphrases him saying data centers are 'more of a local issue' (left out). The Transformer AI campaign finance tracker lists $263,250 from pro-safety super PACs (Jobs and Democracy PAC) supporting his primary; that is outside spending, not his statement. A Route Fifty / City & State article (15 September 2026) on Pennsylvania politicians' reactions to calls for an AI slowdown did not mention him in the version fetched. City & State's 16 October 2026 profile has no AI quotes. As a non-member he could not co-sponsor the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act and did not sign the House letters. Search results for 'Brooks' and AI risk mostly concern roboticist Rodney Brooks, a different person.
